**Mechanism:** context-local proxies. All of them are defined in `src/tessel/globals.py`.

- There is one `ContextVar`, `_app_var` (line 40). It holds the current `AppContext`, which is defined in `src/tessel/ctx.py`.
- Each name is a werkzeug `LocalProxy` bound to that variable. On every access, the proxy reads the `AppContext` that is current for the thread or task, then fetches an attribute from it:
  - `active_app` is `_app_var` → `.app`, the `Tessel` instance (`src/tessel/app.py`). See line 44.
  - `g` is `_app_var` → `.g`, an `_AppCtxGlobals` object (`src/tessel/ctx.py`). See line 47.
  - `request` is `_app_var` → `.request`, a `Request` (`src/tessel/wrappers.py`). See line 57.
  - `session` (line 60) and `app_ctx` (line 41) work the same way. `app_ctx` has no attribute, so it is the context itself.
- Pushing an `AppContext` (for example with `app.app_context()` or while handling a request) sets `_app_var`. Popping it resets the variable.
- If nothing is set, the proxy raises a "Working outside of application context" error. For `request` and `session`, the error says "outside of request context" instead.
- Because the variable is a `ContextVar`, each thread, greenlet or asyncio task sees its own context.
- The request and app contexts have merged into one `AppContext`. The old `request_ctx` name is now a deprecated alias for `app_ctx` (line 65).

I read only `globals.py`. I did not open `ctx.py` to check how it pushes and pops the context.
